findings.finding: Two keyspaces are live and the IRPT builders read BOTH.
findings.measured: The monolith `opal-data-assets` (`{source}/{scope}/silver/{feed}/date=YYYY-MM-DD/data.parquet`, `data/assets/scripts/silver/silver_registry.py`) and the legacy firm buckets `opal-data-bd`, `opal-data-inf`, `opal-data-cot` (`silver/<feed>/<date>.parquet`, flat, plus `gold/canonical/`). `holdings_snapshot.py` reads the monolith for 49F (`schwab/08335338`, `smartx/platform`) and COT (`blackdiamond/cottonwood`) and the LEGACY bucket for INF (`opal-data-inf/silver/api_dims`, `silver/eclipse`; `build_inf`, `INF_SOURCE_BUCKET`). The 49F engine reads the monolith (`runner_common.py` SILVER_BUCKET = opal-data-assets, scope schwab/08335338) and writes gold to `opal-data-49financial`. The LGIC resource registry (`infra/logic/registry/resources.json`, 465 rows) carries no S3 table row of any kind (types are IAM, Lambda, event rules, secrets), so no silver table has a registry address to cite; the gold's address is minted at L4 from `lib/opal_naming.py` (rule 30).

findings.measured: `dim_position` 559 partitions over 558 trading days; 6,347 accounts with positions on 09-25, closing_price non-null on 106,835 of 106,835 rows. `dim_balance` gives the account value (7,548 accounts). findings.finding: The basis Andrew named is implemented NOWHERE measured; the two calculations that exist are both flow-based.
findings.measured: The 49F engine (`c02_twr_engine.py`) links r_net = (emv - bmv - cf) / bmv from `canonical_valuation` and `flow_ledger`, which is how a zero-EMV day with no flow becomes -100% (S177). The three per-firm `account_gains` golds (`data/black_diamond/scripts/gold/B_03.account_gains.py`, `data/cot/.../B_03.account_gains.py`, `data/inf/.../INF_B_03.account_gains.py`, and `runners_49f/c00_account_gains.py`) decompose AUA(t)-AUA(t-1) = growth + NNA with NNA the residual, a transaction-classified identity. Neither computes a weight-pro-rated security return from end-of-day holdings. The nearest surface to Andrew's basis is the per-position price/value columns themselves, which exist on 49F and INF rows and are derivable on COT rows.

findings.finding: The served HoldingsSnapshot already answers 'which accounts, which positions, which values, on which day' per firm, with reconciliation and one identity normalizer.
findings.measured: `data/assets/scripts/gold/investor_reporting/holdings_snapshot.py` with `holdings_49f.py` (Schwab meshed with SmartX), `holdings_inf.py` (Orion meshed with Eclipse) and `build_cot` (BD Rebalancer) resolves per firm the account set, the custody clock, the position rows and the tie of positions to the account value, and mints node ids through `_ids/ids.py` and `_ids/raw_keys.json` (the same normalizer the handlers use, rows W1-S7/W2-S11). It is a one-as-of snapshot, not a series, and it runs ad hoc (the served as-of is 2026-09-22 while every silver is at 09-25 or later; row S152). Its reads are the same reads a daily holdings-basis gold needs.

outcomes.outcome: An advisor at any of the three firms reads, for one account, a daily return series and its period figures computed from that account's own end-of-day holdings only: each day's return is the weight-pro-rated return of the securities it held, weights relative to the account on that day, the delta taken from the previous day, with no inflow or outflow logic (Andrew's call-3 basis, verbatim in the CTO record).
outcomes.note: CANDIDATE THREAD (FWD-1 at L2): a 49 Financial advisor, one invested Schwab account, the YTD window, because 49F has one custody partition per trading day with a closing price on every position (IV.2) and its served figure is the one Andrew has seen wrong (IV.12).

outcomes.outcome: The advisor reads the SAME figure on the Performance page and in the export for every firm, because the page reads ONE gold shape in which the firm is a column, not a code path.

An Opal operator can state, for any firm and any day, which silver table supplied the positions and the values, how many accounts were computable, how many were not, and why (no position row, no price, zero value), from the gold's own manifest rather than from a query.
An advisor is never shown a return for a day whose holdings did not land: an absent day is absent, the page names the last day it has, and nothing rolls forward or fills with zero.

An Opal analyst compares Opal's holdings-basis figure against the vendor's official figure at pre-set periods (Black Diamond for 49F and Cottonwood, Orion for Inflection) and reads the difference with both bases stated, as a bounded check at defined points, never as a standing comparator or a second pipeline.

The gold is produced every trading day on a schedule of its own, and its completion manifest names the silver partitions it consumed, so a missed day and a late day read differently from a completed one.

A security whose price is missing, stale or zero on a day is handled by one stated rule and surfaced on the account's row, never silently priced at zero or dropped; the account's cash and cash-equivalent balances are handled by one stated rule the face can name.

A relationship or client figure composes its accounts' daily returns by the same weight-pro-rated rule, and never by summing or averaging period returns (FWD-3's rule against a fabricated aggregate carries).
